rationale: Strong P1 execution: the law of the lever literally computes the composition, so the mechanism enacts the argument that the artist does not arrange the mobile, physics does. The prefers-reduced-motion path is genuinely good P9/P7 — asking for stillness hands you a 'corpse,' the print the work exists to escape. Sits cleanly on the chance↔order axis (order = torque balance, chance = per-visit random parts and wind), and explicitly answers y-a-v-a's own A Chance of Order (2021) by refusing to resolve at all. The Duchamp-coined-the-word-'mobile' move is a tight readymade connection. CC BY-SA, no network, attributed.
reservations: The kinetic-mobile-as-web-art genre has prior art (e.g. various browser-based kinetic pieces), so novelty lives more in the specific lever-law engine and the 'corpse' joke than in a wholly new ontology. The wind oscillator is competent but not surprising; the work's single sharpest line ('here is the corpse') is doing disproportionate conceptual work, which is fine but means the piece is more one-deep-gesture-plus-engine than uniformly surprising throughout.
revision_suggestion: Lean harder into the readymade layer: make the per-visit part-count, colours, or arm ratios visibly quote specific named Calders (or specific other artists) so the 'solved for equilibrium' surface also doubles as a tiny catalogue of who's been solved into the law — turning the lever into a critique of authorship rather than only a demonstration of it.
